task.title: AI support platform migration
task.scenario: A B2B SaaS company must decide whether to migrate 40 percent of its support workflow to an AI triage platform before the holiday traffic spike.
constraints: The plan must preserve enterprise SLA commitments.
The CFO wants a payback argument and downside case.
Engineering can spare only two developers for six weeks.
Support leadership needs a customer communication plan.
source_packet: Ticket volume is 62,000 per month, with a projected 35 percent holiday spike.
Current median first response time is 11 minutes; SLA breach threshold is 30 minutes.
The vendor pilot resolved 27 percent of tier-1 tickets without human escalation.
False routing during the pilot rose from 3.1 percent to 5.4 percent.
Enterprise customers represent 38 percent of ticket volume and 71 percent of ARR.
Security review found no critical blockers, but audit logging needs extra work.
The support team has two enablement slots before the holiday freeze.
task.deliverable: A go/no-go recommendation with staged rollout, financial case, engineering plan, risk controls, and customer-facing communication guidance.
success_criteria: The plan distinguishes facts, estimates, and assumptions.
At least two risks have mitigations and rollback triggers.
Final prose is coherent enough for executives.

- 62,000 tickets/month with a 35% holiday spike.
- AI pilot resolved 27% of tier-1 tickets autonomously.

### Estimates and Assumptions
- Autonomous resolution rates vary ±7% around pilot mean (20%-35%).
- False routing may increase linearly with scaling of AI platform use.
- SLA breach due to false routing could cause revenue impact up to 4% ARR loss.
- Engineering capacity constraints may delay audit logging by up to 40%. Rollback triggered if delays exceed 20%.

### Sensitivity Analysis
- Payback ROI materially sensitive to autonomous resolution rate; at 20% resolution, financial benefits decrease by ~25%.
- False routing rate impacts SLA breach probability and costs; higher false routing (>5%) increases risk of revenue-impacting SLA breaches.

### Financial Payback Case
- Labor cost savings from 20-27% AI resolution reduce support FTE burden.
- Holiday capacity increased to absorb 35% ticket volume spike while preserving SLA.
- Engineering and enablement costs accounted for 2 developers × 6 weeks + support training.

- SLA breaches triggered by elevated false routing cause revenue loss estimated up to 4% ARR.
- Increased manual re-routing and remediation add support costs (~15% incremental workload).
- Potential delays in audit logging increase compliance risk and warrant rollback.

- **False routing SLA breach**: Daily SLA performance monitoring; rollback triggered if SLA breach rate attributable to false routing exceeds 3% increase over baseline for 3 consecutive days.
